info.title: Jellyfin Canopy — Platform v1
info.description:
This document is AUTHORED, not generated from the running server. Generating it from the code would document whatever the code happens to do, mistakes included, and would make a breaking change undetectable — the spec would simply move with the bug. Here the spec is the source of truth and the server is checked against it by PlatformContractTests.

Only routes under /JellyfinCanopy/Platform/v1 are described. The pre-platform /JellyfinCanopy/* routes are compatibility surfaces with their own shapes and are deliberately absent; they are never promoted into the platform implicitly.

Platform responses use application/json. An absent Accept header, application/json, application/*, or */* permits that representation; a malformed, over-bound, or excluding Accept header receives a structured 406 after any required authorization. Body-bearing requests accept application/json only; a different or missing Content-Type is a structured 415 after authorization. Request readers ignore unknown object properties, reject unknown enum values as invalid_request, and require RFC 3339 UTC timestamps with an explicit UTC offset. GUIDs use lowercase canonical D form. Clients must ignore unknown response properties so additive v1 evolution remains usable.

Changes within v1 are additive only (ADR-0010). Removing a path, removing a required property, or changing a property's type is a v2 concern, and contracts/platform/v1/frozen.json exists so CI can prove it rather than a reviewer having to notice.

servers.description: The configured Jellyfin server base, including any reverse-proxy base path. Resolve Platform paths beneath this base rather than resetting to the bare origin.

get.summary: Whether the platform is present, and which protocol versions it speaks.
get.description:
The ONLY anonymous route in Platform v1. A client must be able to learn whether the native platform is serving requests before it has a reason to authenticate, and probing this reveals nothing an unauthenticated caller could not learn by noticing the plugin is installed. Available=false means the administrator has disabled Platform v1; the protocol range remains present so a client can distinguish a disabled compatible host from an unknown route. Disabled discovery responses use Cache-Control: no-store.

The payload is deliberately uninteresting: no users, no installed extensions, no topology, no configuration, no server identity. Adding a property here widens what an unauthenticated caller learns.

200.description: The platform discovery representation. Check Available before authenticating or using another Platform route.

Cache-Control.description: Present as no-store when Available is false, so disabled state is never retained as a reusable representation.

get.summary: The highest protocol version both sides speak.
get.description:
A client offers the range it supports; the host answers with what it will actually use.

No overlap is reported as a 200 with compatible=false, NOT as an error. A negotiation that concludes "no common version" has succeeded — it answered the question asked — and a client renders that differently from "unavailable" and from "denied". Collapsing the three would make a version mismatch indistinguishable from a permissions problem.

A client that supplies no range is treated as speaking the oldest protocol only. Assuming it supports the newest would be optimistic about software the host knows nothing about.

parameters.name: protocolMinimum
parameters.description: Lowest protocol version the client supports. Defaults to the host's minimum.

parameters.name: protocolMaximum
parameters.description: Highest protocol version the client supports. Defaults to the host's minimum, not its maximum.

200.description: Negotiation completed. Check compatible before using protocol.

post.summary: Resolve the current actor's bounded native item-detail contributions.
post.description: Canopy re-authorizes the Jellyfin item and composes only the fixed Spoiler Guard, Hidden Content, and Seerr pilot families. Unknown or unavailable families are omitted. The response is capped at twelve contributions, retaining bounded headroom for another native-safe family. Opaque prepare handles carry no client-interpretable authority. This POST receives a strong ETag over its exact response bytes, but intentionally has no conditional-GET or 304 behavior because the bounded client capability body is part of the representation key.

200.description: The current authorized native contribution catalog, including an empty catalog when no pilot family applies.

post.summary: Re-authorize an opaque catalog action and mint a short-lived invocation capability.
post.description: The prepare handle is resolved only for the current Jellyfin user. Canopy rechecks the user, item, configuration, feature state, client field support, and owner authorization before returning a bounded native form. Expired, restarted, cross-user, stale, or unauthorized handles are deliberately indistinguishable as not_found.

200.description: A short-lived capability and bounded native form for one exact prepared action.

post.summary: Invoke one prepared first-party action through Canopy's fixed dispatcher.
post.description: The idempotency key is carried exactly once in the JSON body; the Idempotency-Key header is forbidden on this route. Canopy consumes the opaque capability only after fresh Jellyfin and owning-service authorization, validates answers against the server-bound form and feature variant, and executes only one of the three fixed pilot ports. Clients must treat refresh targets as allowlisted hints and ignore unknown targets.

200.description: A stored semantic action outcome. A replay returns the same semantic body.

PlatformEntityTag.description: A strong validator derived from SHA-256 over the exact Platform JSON response bytes.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745 structured-field date announcing when the operation was deprecated. Present only for operations listed in deprecations.json.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594 HTTP-date naming the earliest time the deprecated operation may be removed, subject also to the Canopy release window.

JellyfinToken.name: Authorization
JellyfinToken.description: Jellyfin's own scheme: `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="<token>"`. EP-00 verified that the 10.x `?api_key=` query parameter has been removed in Jellyfin 12, while `?apikey=` and `?ApiKey=` still work; the platform documents only the header because a credential in a query string lands in logs and referrers.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: Optional strong precondition. A wildcard or bounded entity-tag list is accepted; weak tags do not match the current representation.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: Optional cache revalidation precondition. A wildcard or bounded entity-tag list is accepted and compared weakly.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Reusable header carrier for future Platform mutation routes. One case-sensitive value identifies a retry together with the authenticated acting user and operation. The native actions/invoke route deliberately uses the same bounded value in its JSON body and forbids this header, so that route does not reference this component.

BareUnauthorized.description: No or invalid credentials. EP-00 measured that Jellyfin 12 returns this with ZERO body bytes, so it carries no platform error envelope — the envelope applies only after authorization succeeds (ADR-0002). A client must not attempt to parse this body.

BareForbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted. Zero body bytes, for the same reason as 401.

PayloadTooLarge.description: A kernel-owned request bound was exceeded. The message names which axis, so a client knows whether to send fewer items, shorter strings, or a flatter shape.

InvalidRequest.description: The authenticated JSON request is malformed, incomplete, duplicated, self-contradictory, or uses an unsupported protocol or surface schema.

NotFound.description: The item, opaque handle, capability, action, or current authorization is unavailable. The same response deliberately covers absent, expired, stale, cross-user, and denied resources.

InternalError.description: An internal failure occurred after authorization. No provider, host, path, credential, or exception detail crosses the platform boundary.

Unavailable.description: Platform v1 is administratively disabled, or a required first-party owner or provider is temporarily unavailable. The response is retryable; clients must keep ordinary Jellyfin behavior usable. Administrative-gate responses include Cache-Control: no-store, while an owner/provider failure is not required to include that optional header.

Cache-Control.description: Present as no-store when the administrative availability gate selected this response.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The same bounded correlation identifier carried in the PlatformError body.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The authenticated request carries a body with a missing or non-JSON Content-Type.

NotAcceptable.description: The Accept header is malformed, exceeds the negotiation bounds, or excludes the application/json representation returned by Platform v1.

Timeout.description: Model binding or action execution exceeded the fixed 30-second Platform v1 deadline. The deadline is cooperative and excludes bounded body acquisition and result serialization.

NotModified.description: The current representation weakly matches If-None-Match. The response has no body.

InvalidConditionalRequest.description: A conditional header is malformed or exceeds the Platform parser bounds.

IdempotencyConflict.description: A mutation key was reused with different semantics, or a prior execution is indeterminate. Returned as non-retryable 409 conflict.

IdempotencyAtCapacity.description: The bounded process-local idempotency store or follower budget cannot admit work. Rejected before mutation execution as retryable 429 rate_limited.

PreconditionFailed.description: No strong If-Match candidate matches the current representation.

Id.description: The non-empty Jellyfin item id. Canopy resolves it again under the current actor.

ContributionKinds.description: Recognized v1 values are action and status. Unknown values are ignored.

FieldKinds.description: Recognized v1 values are confirmation, boolean, single_select, and multi_select. Unknown values are ignored.

InputModes.description: The native item-detail pilot requires dpad. Unknown values are ignored.

Accessibility.description: Recognized v1 value is screen_reader. Unknown values are ignored.

CatalogRevision.description: A process-keyed revision of the caller-visible semantic catalog. Prepare-handle rotation does not change it.

PlatformNativeContribution.description: Flat discriminated wire shape. action requires SemanticIcon and Enabled and requires PrepareHandle when enabled; status requires Tone. A client must omit an unknown Kind rather than inventing behavior.

PlatformActionAnswer.description: Exactly one of BooleanValue and OptionIds is present. Field ids are unique within one invocation.

Targets.description: Known Android targets are jellyfin_item and item_detail_surface. Unknown targets are ignored.

Available.description: Whether the platform is present and serving.

ProtocolMinimum.description: Lowest protocol version this host speaks.

ProtocolMaximum.description: Highest protocol version this host speaks.

Compatible.description: Whether the client and host ranges overlap at all.

Protocol.description: The agreed version. Meaningless when compatible is false.

HostProtocolMinimum.description: Echoed so a client can report a mismatch usefully rather than just failing.

HostProtocolMaximum.description: Echoed so a client can report a mismatch usefully rather than just failing.

SeerrAvailable.description: Whether the authenticated Jellyfin user currently has a usable, non-blocked Seerr link. Seerr operations repeat their authorization checks before use.

PlatformError.description: The single Platform v1 error envelope, returned for every failure that occurs after authorization has succeeded. Deliberately a superset of the richest legacy shape ({ error, code, message }) so an adapter presenting a platform failure to a legacy consumer drops fields rather than translating them.

Error.description: Always true. Carried so a consumer that already branches on a truthy error keeps working through an adapter.

Message.description: Human-readable and safe to display. May be reworded or translated at any time, so it is never the thing a consumer branches on.

Retryable.description: Whether retrying the identical request could plausibly succeed. Derived from the code rather than chosen per endpoint, so two endpoints cannot disagree about the same code.

CorrelationId.description: Ties this response to the server log lines for the same request. Also returned in the X-Correlation-Id header. Generated by the host and never accepted from the caller.

PlatformErrorCode.description: Machine-readable failure code. Branch on this, never on the message. An unfamiliar code must be treated as a generic failure of its HTTP status class, which is why each code maps to exactly one status.

PlatformEntityTag.description: A quoted, opaque strong SHA-256 representation validator.
